claims.text: The memorandum's five numbered paragraphs read: '1. At 290200 EST AFOC informed NMCC that an unidentified helicopter, possibly two, had been sighted flying low over Loring AFB Maine, in proximity to a weapons storage area. 2. An Army National Guard helo was called in to assist in locating the unidentified helo(s). 3. NORAD was informed of the incident by SAC, requested and received authority from Canadian officials to proceed into Canadian airspace if necessary to locate the intruder. 4. At 0404 SAC Command Center informed NMCC that the army helo assisting on the scene had not sighted the unidentified helo(s). 5. A similar incident was reported at Loring the evening of 28 October 1975.' Signed C. D. Roberts, Jr., Brigadier General, USMC, Deputy Director for Operations (NMCC).

claims.text: THE DOCUMENT NEVER SAYS UFO. Its vocabulary throughout is 'unidentified helicopter', 'intruder' and 'AFB Penetration'. What it documents is a failure to identify and a failure to intercept at a nuclear weapons storage area, escalated to the Joint Staff, the Army Staff, a Deputy Secretary of Defense aide and the State Department's Canadian desk. That is the whole of the Tier 1 claim and it is enough.

desc: THE BEST SINGLE DOCUMENT IN THE NUCLEAR STRAND AND IT IS NOT A UFO DOCUMENT. It is a National Military Command Center Memorandum for Record, dated 29 October 1975 at 0605 EST, subject line 'AFB Penetration', signed C. D. Roberts, Jr., Brigadier General, USMC, Deputy Director for Operations. Five numbered paragraphs record that an unidentified helicopter, possibly two, was sighted flying low over Loring AFB in proximity to a weapons storage area; that an Army National Guard helicopter was called in and failed to locate it; that NORAD requested and received authority from Canadian officials to cross into Canadian airspace in pursuit; and that a similar incident had occurred the previous evening. Four DDO updates follow, each citing its source message. The distribution list is what makes the document remarkable: CJCS in five copies, DJS in three, J-30 through J-38, the Chief of Staff of the Army, the Chief of Naval Operations, the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, the Commandant of the Marine Corps, the Chief of WWMCCS Operations and Evaluation Division, the DIA representative for the National Military Intelligence Center, the NSA representative, the CIA representative and the Western Hemisphere desk. This is what a nuclear security incident looks like on paper when nobody has decided what it is.

timeline.label: NMCC logs an 'AFB Penetration' at Loring and runs it up the Joint Staff
timeline.text: At 0605 EST on 29 October 1975 the National Military Command Center issued a Memorandum for Record subject 'AFB Penetration', signed C. D. Roberts, Jr., Brigadier General, USMC, Deputy Director for Operations, recording that an unidentified helicopter, possibly two, had been sighted flying low over Loring AFB in proximity to a weapons storage area, that an Army National Guard helicopter had failed to locate it, and that NORAD had obtained Canadian authority to pursue across the border. Distribution ran to CJCS, DJS, J-30 through J-38, the service chiefs and the DIA, NSA and CIA representatives.

unverified: The memorandum was NOT OPENED as a scanned facsimile by this board; it was read as NICAP's transcription of the released document. The transcription carries the signature block as '//signed//', which is how a released copy renders a signature, and its internal source-message citations are consistent throughout.
